headline: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO after a dual-affair scandal, as Nvidia privately confirmed to Congress it could track chips to fight smuggling to China and an OpenAI board member warned of a high risk of AI takeover within three years.

points.text: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO after the company's board investigated two extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy; longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

MIT Technology Review reported that Nvidia privately confirmed to a member of Congress it could technically track chips to fight smuggling to China, even as the industry publicly questioned the feasibility of such measures.
The White House is standing by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick despite a view within the administration that he delayed action on chip smuggling to China.
CSET examined different potential implementations of 'AI kill switches,' a tool policymakers have proposed requiring to quickly stop or limit the impact of a harmful AI incident.
An OpenAI board member warned of a high risk of AI takeover within three years, saying AIs are already improving AIs and that action is needed now.
AI Frontiers argued the AI safety field is failing to evaluate how biologists could misuse AI, warning that experts assisted by AI could be far more dangerous than novices.
